rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet said Quraysh questioned his night journey; God displayed Jerusalem to him so he could answer their questions despite not having memorized its details.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لقد رأيتني في الحجر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet described meeting Moses, Jesus, and Abraham praying, leading them in prayer, and being greeted by Malik, keeper of the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقد رأيتني في جماعة من الأنبياء، وإذا موسى قائم يصلي، وإذا هو رجل ضرب جعد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report of the ascent shows usurers with house-sized bellies and visible snakes inside them.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء أكلة الربا، فلما نزلت إلى السماء الدنيا نظرت أسفل مني فإذا أنا برهج ودخان

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet said devils create smoke, noise, and distractions before human eyes to prevent reflection on the dominion of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: هذه الشياطين يحرفون على أعين بني آدم ألا يتفكرون في ملكوت السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
rows.claim: A long composite report about the Isra includes the number of steps and angels; al-Hakim says its contents are unobjectionable as divine power if the report is sound.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب وعبد الله (11) بن عباس -ومحمد بن إسحاق بن يسار،

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says the previously cited report of Abu Harun al-Abdi is sufficient to establish the Isra and Mi'raj.
rows.anchor: قال البيهقي: فيما ذكرنا قبل في حديث أبي هارون العبدي في إثبات الإسراء والمعراج كفاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that multiple Successors and leading exegetes also transmitted the Isra report in mursal form.
rows.anchor: وقد أرسل هذا الحديث غير واحد من التابعين وأئمة المفسرين

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that some believers apostatized after hearing of the journey; Abu Bakr affirmed it, saying he believed even more extraordinary reports from heaven, and was called al-Siddiq.
rows.anchor: عن عروة، عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، قالت: لما أسري بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المسجد الأقصى

rows.speaker: أم هانئ
rows.claim: Um Hani says the Prophet prayed the night prayer at her home, then told her he prayed at Jerusalem and returned for dawn prayer with them.
rows.anchor: عن أم هانئ بنت أبي طالب [رضي الله عنها] (6) في مسرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنها كانت تقول: ما أسري برسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls al-Kalbi, the transmitter in Ibn Ishaq's route from Abu Salih to Um Hani, wholly abandoned and extremely unreliable.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: متروك بمرة ساقط،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ya'la transmits a fuller version through a different route from Yahya ibn Abi Amr al-Saybani, from Abu Salih, from Um Hani.
rows.anchor: لكن رواه أبو يعلى في مسنده عن محمد بن إسماعيل الأنصاري، عن ضمرة بن ربيعة،

rows.speaker: أم هانئ
rows.claim: In a report from Um Hani, Gabriel brought a mount between mule and donkey size and carried the Prophet to Jerusalem, where he saw Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and the one-eyed Dajjal.
rows.anchor: فإذا على الباب دابة دون البغل وفوق الحمار، فحملني عليها، ثم انطلق حتى انتهى بي إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: أم هانئ
rows.claim: Um Hani warned the Prophet that Quraysh would deny him and might attack him, but he went out and told them what he had seen.
rows.anchor: إني أذكرك (1) الله، إنك تأتي قوما يكذبونك وينكرون مقالتك، فأخاف أن يسطوا بك.

rows.speaker: أم هانئ
rows.claim: The Prophet answered questions about caravans, including a lost camel, a broken red camel and a water bowl he had drunk from; the caravans arrived as predicted.
rows.anchor: قال: "نعم، والله قد وجدتهم أضلوا بعيرا لهم فهم في طلبه".

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr confirmed that he had placed the bowl and that nobody else drank from it; he believed the Prophet and was then called al-Siddiq.
rows.anchor: قال: أبو بكر: أنا والله وضعتها فما شربها أحد، ولا أهراقوه في الأرض. فصدقه أبو بكر [رضي الله عنه] (7) وآمن به، فسمي يومئذ الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken together, sound, fair, and weak reports establish one night journey from Mecca to Jerusalem; variations reflect narrators' differing wording, additions, omissions, and fallibility.
rows.anchor: يحصل مضمون ما اتفقت عليه من مسرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من مكة إلى بيت المقدس، وأنه مرة واحدة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects treating each discrepant account as a separate journey, calling that an implausible evasion that solves nothing.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل من الناس كل رواية خالفت الأخرى مرة على حدة، فأثبت إسراءات متعددة فقد أبعد وأغرب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects a later proposal of three separate journeys; the view is unreported from the early generations, and repeated events would have been taught and transmitted as such.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد جدا، ولم ينقل هذا عن أحد من السلف، ولو تعدد هذا التعدد لأخبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم به أمته،

rows.speaker: موسى بن عقبة عن الزهري وعروة
rows.claim: Musa ibn Uqba, transmitting from al-Zuhri, and Urwa place the Isra one year before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: قال موسى بن عقبة، عن الزهري: كان الإسراء قبل الهجرة بسنة. وكذا قال عروة.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi dates the Isra to sixteen months before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: بستة عشر شهرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir's preferred account is a waking bodily journey from Mecca to Jerusalem on the Buraq, followed by prayer in the mosque and ascent through the seven heavens.
rows.anchor: والحق أنه، عليه السلام (12) أسري به يقظة لا مناما من مكة إلى بيت المقدس، راكبا البراق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent passed through the heavens, where angels and prophets greeted Muhammad; he met Moses in the sixth heaven and Abraham in the seventh before reaching the point where the pens' scratching was heard.
rows.anchor: حتى مر بموسى الكليم في السادسة، وإبراهيم الخليل في السابعة، ثم جاوز منزلتهما صلى الله عليه وسلم وعليهما وعلى سائر الأنبياء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He saw the Sidrat al-Muntaha, Gabriel with six hundred wings, the green rafraf, the Frequented House with Abraham, and Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: ورأى سدرة المنتهى وغشيها من أمر الله، تعالى، عظمة عظيمة، من فراش من ذهب، وألوان متعددة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed fifty prayers during the ascent and reduced them to five as mercy; Ibn Kathir sees this as a great indication of prayer's honor and importance.
rows.anchor: وفرض الله [عز وجل] (5) عليه هنالك الصلوات خمسين، ثم خففها إلى خمس؛ رحمة منه ولطفا بعباده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prevailing reports say Muhammad led the prophets in prayer at Jerusalem after descending; reports placing the prayer in heaven are fewer, and its timing may have been dawn.
rows.anchor: والذي تظاهرت به الروايات أنه بيت المقدس، ولكن في بعضها أنه كان أول (6) دخوله إليه. والظاهر أنه بعد رجوعه إليه؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir argues the congregational prayer was after the return from the upper realm: the prophets gathered then, and Gabriel indicated that Muhammad should lead them, displaying his superiority.
rows.anchor: ثم لما فرغ من الذي أريد به، اجتمع هو وإخوانه من النبيين [صلوات الله وسلامه عليه وعليهم أجمعين] (7) ثم أظهر شرفه وفضله عليهم بتقديمه في الإمامة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After leaving Jerusalem, the Prophet rode the Buraq back to Mecca before daybreak.
rows.anchor: ثم خرج من بيت المقدس فركب البراق وعاد إلى مكة بغلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports variously place the offered vessels of milk, honey, and wine in Jerusalem or heaven; Ibn Kathir allows both locations as hospitality for the arriving guest.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون هاهنا وهاهنا؛ لأنه كالضيافة للقادم، والله أعلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars hold that the Prophet was taken bodily and spiritually while awake, and Ibn Kathir supports this reading over a spirit-only journey.
rows.anchor: فالأكثرون من العلماء على أنه أسري ببدنه وروحه يقظة لا مناما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that the Quran's opening glorification signals a tremendous event; if it were only a dream, Quraysh would not have regarded it as extraordinary or rejected it.
rows.anchor: فالتسبيح إنما يكون عند الأمور العظام، ولو كان مناما لم يكن فيه كبير شيء ولم يكن مستعظما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word servant refers to the whole person, body and spirit, and the Quran says God journeyed with His servant.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإن العبد عبارة عن مجموع الروح والجسد، وقد قال [عز شأنه] (1) {أسرى بعبده ليلا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the vision in 17:60 as an eyewitness vision shown to the Prophet on the night of the Isra; al-Bukhari transmits this report.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس [رضي الله عنهما] (2) هي رؤيا عين أريها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's statement that sight did not swerve supports a bodily event because sight is an instrument of the self; riding the Buraq likewise indicates a bodily journey.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى: {ما زاغ البصر وما طغى} [النجم: 17] ، والبصر من آلات الذات لا الروح.

rows.speaker: معاوية بن أبي سفيان
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports Muawiya's view that the Prophet's night journey was a true vision from God.
rows.anchor: أن معاوية بن أبي سفيان [رضي الله عنهما] (5) كان إذا سئل عن مسرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: كانت رؤيا من الله صادقة.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha is reported to have said that the Prophet's body was not missing and that only his spirit was taken on the journey.
rows.anchor: وحدثني بعض آل أبي بكر أن عائشة كانت تقول: ما فقد جسد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولكن أسري بروحه.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq did not reject Aisha's statement, citing al-Hasan's interpretation of 17:60 and God's revelation to Abraham in a dream; prophetic revelation can come awake or asleep.
rows.anchor: فعرفت أن الوحي يأتي للأنبياء من الله أيقاظا ونياما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the Prophet described his eyes sleeping while his heart remained awake, and leaves open whether he was asleep or awake; either way, what he saw from God was true.
rows.anchor: فكان (7) رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "تنام عيناي، وقلبي يقظان" فالله أعلم أي ذلك كان قد جاءه،

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن جرير
rows.claim: Al-Tabari sharply rejects Ibn Ishaq's spirit-only interpretation as contrary to the Quran's apparent wording and cites the bodily-journey arguments.
rows.anchor: وقد تعقبه أبو جعفر بن جرير في تفسيره بالرد والإنكار والتشنيع، بأن هذا خلاف (9) ظاهر سياق القرآن،

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: A report transmitted by al-Waqidi says Abu Sufyan tried to discredit Muhammad before Heraclius by describing the Isra as an impossible claim, but the Jerusalem priest corroborated it.
rows.anchor: من طريق محمد بن عمر الواقدي: حدثني مالك بن أبي الرجال، عن عمرو بن عبد الله، عن محمد بن كعب القرظي،

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان
rows.claim: Abu Sufyan admitted that, although he wanted to discredit Muhammad to Heraclius, he avoided making a false claim for fear it would be exposed.
rows.anchor: قال في هذا السياق عن أبي سفيان: والله ما يمنعني أن أقول عليه قولا أسقطه من عينه إلا أني أكره أن أكذب عنده

rows.speaker: بطريق إيلياء
rows.claim: The Jerusalem priest said the mosque's locked door resisted the workers that night; in the morning they found a stone bored with the trace of a mount's tether.
rows.anchor: فإذا الحجر الذي في زاوية الباب (3) مثقوب، وإذا فيه أثر مربط الدابة

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب عمر بن دحية
rows.claim: Ibn Dihya says Isra reports are mutawatir from many Companions, including Umar, Ali, Ibn Masud, Abu Dharr, Abu Hurayra, Ibn Abbas, and Aisha.
rows.anchor: وقد تواترت الروايات في حديث الإسراء عن عمر بن الخطاب، وعلي [بن أبي طالب] (5) وابن مسعود، وأبي ذر، ومالك بن صعصعة،

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب عمر بن دحية
rows.claim: Although not every Companion's report meets the highest soundness criteria, Muslims agree on the Isra, while heretics object to it.
rows.anchor: وإن لم تكن (7) رواية بعضهم على شرط الصحة، فحديث الإسراء أجمع عليه المسلمون، واعترض فيه الزنادقة الملحدون (8)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir invokes the promise that God will complete His light despite the disbelievers' opposition.
rows.anchor: يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم والله متم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the Isra of Muhammad, the Quran turns to Moses; Ibn Kathir notes that the Quran often pairs the two prophets and the Torah with the Quran.
rows.anchor: فإنه تعالى كثيرا ما يقرن بين ذكر موسى ومحمد عليهما السلام (2) وبين ذكر التوراة والقرآن؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book given to Moses is the Torah, made guidance for the Israelites, and its instruction is not to take a guardian, helper, or object of worship besides God.
rows.anchor: {وجعلناه} أي الكتاب {هدى} أي هاديا {لبني إسرائيل ألا تتخذوا} أي لئلا تتخذوا {من دوني وكيلا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent every prophet with the command to worship Him alone without a partner.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى أنزل على كل نبي أرسله (3) أن يعبده وحده لا شريك له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Descendants of those carried with Noah” is a vocative that recalls God's favor and urges Noah's descendants to emulate him and remember God's sending Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فيه تهييج وتنبيه على المنة، أي: يا سلالة من نجينا فحملنا مع نوح في السفينة، تشبهوا بأبيكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was called a grateful servant because he praised God for food, drink, clothing, and all his affairs.
rows.anchor: أن نوحا، عليه السلام، كان يحمد الله [تعالى] (4) على طعامه وشرابه ولباسه وشأنه كله;

rows.speaker: سعد بن مسعود الثقفي
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Masud says Noah was called grateful because he praised God whenever he ate or drank.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سنان، عن سعد بن مسعود الثقفي قال: إنما سمي نوح عبدا شكورا؛ لأنه كان إذا أكل أو شرب حمد الله

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet said God is pleased with a servant who praises Him after eating a meal or drinking.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله ليرضى عن العبد أن يأكل الأكلة أو يشرب الشربة فيحمد الله عليها".

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Noah praised God in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك، عن زيد بن أسلم: كان يحمد الله على كل حال.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the intercession report, people ask Noah for help because he was the first messenger to earth and God named him a grateful servant.
rows.anchor: فيأتون نوحا فيقولون: يا نوح، أنت (8) أول الرسل إلى أهل الأرض، وقد سماك الله عبدا شكورا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had already informed the Israelites in their revealed Book that they would twice spread corruption and become greatly arrogant; “decreed” means He advanced and foretold it.
rows.anchor: أي: تقدم إليهم وأخبرهم في الكتاب الذي أنزله عليهم أنهم سيفسدون في الأرض مرتين ويعلون (1) علوا كبيرا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the first corruption, God sent a powerful, equipped force that moved freely through Israelite lands and homes, fulfilling the promised punishment.
rows.anchor: أي: سلطنا عليكم جندا من خلقنا أولي بأس شديد، أي: قوة وعدة وسلطة (2) شديدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada identify the attackers as Goliath and his troops; David later killed Goliath, allowing the Israelites to regain the advantage.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس وقتادة: أنه جالوت الجزري وجنوده، سلط عليهم أولا ثم أديلوا عليه بعد ذلك.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies the invader as Sennacherib, king of Mosul, and his troops.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير: أنه ملك الموصل سنجاريب وجنوده.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
rows.claim: Another view attributed to Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others identifies the attacker as Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا، وعن غيره: أنه بختنصر ملك بابل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim relates a story in which Nebuchadnezzar rises from a poor, disabled beggar to kingship and then kills many Israelites in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن أبي حاتم له قصة عجيبة في كيفية ترقيه من حال إلى حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir declares Ibn Jarir's long, marfu report from Hudhayfa about the invasion fabricated; al-Mizzi also marked it as a lie.
rows.anchor: وهو حديث موضوع لا محالة، لا يستريب في ذلك من عنده أدنى معرفة بالحديث!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He declines to expand on many Israelite reports because some are fabricated and others merely possible; the Quran itself sufficiently explains the punishment for Israelite tyranny and killing prophets.
rows.anchor: وفيما قص الله تعالى علينا في كتابه غنية عما سواه من بقية الكتب قبله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib reports that Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Jerusalem, killed Israelites, then killed seventy thousand at Damascus around a boiling blood heap until it stopped; Ibn Kathir calls the report sound to Sa'id.
rows.anchor: فقتل على ذلك الدم سبعين ألفا من المسلمين وغيرهم، فسكن (1) . وهذا صحيح إلى سعيد بن المسيب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Nebuchadnezzar killed Israel's leading scholars, left no one who memorized the Torah, and carried many captives away, including descendants of prophets.
rows.anchor: وأنه قتل أشرافهم وعلماءهم، حتى إنه لم يبق من يحفظ التوراة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing good benefits the doer, while wrongdoing harms the wrongdoer, as in the parallel statement in Fussilat.
rows.anchor: أي: فعليها، كما قال تعالى: {من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها} [فصلت: 46] .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the second punishment, enemies would humiliate and overpower the Israelites, enter Jerusalem as before, and thoroughly destroy what they controlled.
rows.anchor: أي: إذا أفسدتم المرة الثانية وجاء أعداؤكم {ليسوءوا وجوهكم} أي: يهينوكم ويقهروكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show mercy by turning the attackers away, but if the Israelites return to corruption, He will again give their enemies power and reserve punishment for the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: أي: متى عدتم إلى الإفساد {عدنا} إلى الإدالة عليكم في الدنيا مع ما ندخره لكم في الآخرة من العذاب والنكال، ولهذا قال [تعالى] (3)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “حصيرا” describes Hell as a place of confinement, an abode and prison from which the disbelievers cannot escape.
rows.anchor: أي: مستقرا ومحصرا وسجنا لا محيد لهم عنه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “حصيرا” as a prison.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس [رضي الله عنهما] (4) : {حصيرا} أي: سجنا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the disbelievers as being confined in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يحصرون فيها.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets “حصيرا” as a bed and resting place.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: فراش ومهاد.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Israel again corrupted, so God empowered Muhammad and his Companions over them to take jizya while they were humbled.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: قد عاد بنو إسرائيل، فسلط الله عليهم هذا الحي، محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه، يأخذون منهم الجزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir praises the Quran as guiding people to the soundest path and clearest way, and as promising a great Resurrection reward to believers who do righteous deeds according to it.
rows.anchor: بأنه يهدي لأقوم الطرق، وأوضح السبل {ويبشر المؤمنين} به {الذين يعملون الصالحات} على مقتضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran warns those who disbelieve in the Hereafter that they will receive painful punishment on Resurrection Day, echoing 3:21.
rows.anchor: {وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة} أي: ويبشر الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة أن {لهم عذابا أليما} أي: يوم القيامة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People sometimes invoke death, destruction, or a curse against themselves, their children, or property; if God answered, they would perish, as 10:11 says.
rows.anchor: {بالشر} أي: بالموت أو الهلاك والدمار واللعنة ونحو ذلك، فلو استجاب له ربه لهلك بدعائه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada explain the harmful invocation as a person praying for evil against himself or what belongs to him.
rows.anchor: وكذا فسره ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وقد تقدم في الحديث:

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report warns people not to pray against themselves or their property, lest their curse coincide with an hour of divine response.
rows.anchor: "لا تدعوا على أنفسكم ولا على أموالكم، أن توافقوا من الله ساعة إجابة يستجيب فيها"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human haste and anxiety drive these destructive prayers.
rows.anchor: وإنما يحمل ابن آدم على ذلك عجلته وقلقه

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي وابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Salman and Ibn Abbas says Adam sneezed and praised God as his soul reached his head; he tried to stand before it reached his legs and asked God to hurry.
rows.anchor: فلما وصلت إلى دماغه عطس، فقال: الحمد لله. فقال الله: يرحمك ربك يا آدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night allows rest while daylight enables livelihoods, crafts, work, and travel; their alternation lets people count days, weeks, months, years, and deadlines for transactions and worship.
rows.anchor: ليسكنوا في الليل وينتشروا في النهار للمعايش والصناعات (3) والأعمال والأسفار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing lengths and qualities of night and day make the passage of time and reckoning possible; a single unchanging span would conceal such measures.
rows.anchor: فإنه لو كان الزمان كله نسقا واحدا وأسلوبا متساويا لما عرف شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dark night, with the moon appearing, and the bright day, with the sun appearing, are distinct signs; the sun is brighter than the moon.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى جعل لليل آية، أي: علامة يعرف بها (1) وهي الظلام وظهور القمر فيه، وللنهار علامة،

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir transmits Ibn Kathir's interpretation that the erased night sign is night darkness and the day's sign is its twilight.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج، عن عبد الله بن كثير في قوله: {فمحونا آية الليل وجعلنا آية النهار مبصرة} قال: ظلمة الليل وسدفة (4) النهار.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the sun is the day sign and the moon the night sign; the erased mark is the moon's dark patch, which God created there.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج عن مجاهد: الشمس آية النهار، والقمر آية الليل {فمحونا آية الليل} قال: السواد الذي في القمر،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the moon once shone like the sun; its dark patch is the erasure of the night sign.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان القمر يضيء كما تضيء الشمس، والقمر آية الليل، والشمس آية النهار

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwa asked about the mark on the moon, Ali identified it as the erased sign mentioned in the verse.
rows.anchor: وقد روى أبو جعفر بن جرير من طرق متعددة جيدة: أن ابن الكواء سأل [أمير المؤمنين] (6) علي ابن أبي طالب فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين، ما هذه اللطخة التي في القمر؟

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the moon's black patch is the erased night sign; the day sign is luminous, and the sun was created brighter and larger than the moon.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {فمحونا آية الليل} كنا نحدث أن (7) محو آية الليل سواد القمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains that God created night and day as the two signs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح عن ابن عباس: {وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين} قال: ليلا ونهارا، كذلك خلقهما الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and other early interpreters explain a person's “bird” as all his good and bad deeds, which remain attached to him for recompense.
rows.anchor: وطائره: هو ما طار عنه من عمله، كما قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وغير واحد: من خير وشر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every deed, small or great, is preserved and written down day and night.
rows.anchor: والمقصود أن عمل ابن آدم محفوظ عليه، قليله وكثيره، ويكتب عليه ليلا ونهارا، صباحا ومساء.

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A report from Jabir has the Prophet say each person's bird is tied to his neck; Ibn Luhay'a glosses “bird” as augury, which Ibn Kathir calls very strange.
rows.anchor: لطائر كل إنسان في عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Resurrection Day the person's entire record is assembled in an open book, received in the right hand if fortunate and the left if wretched; everyone can read it, literate or not.
rows.anchor: أي: نجمع له عمله كله في كتاب يعطاه يوم القيامة، إما بيمينه إن كان سعيدا، أو بشماله إن كان شقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person can serve as his own accountant because he knows he was not wronged and remembers what he did; nothing but his own deeds was recorded against him.
rows.anchor: أي: إنك (3) تعلم أنك لم تظلم ولم يكتب عليك غير ما عملت؛ لأنك ذكرت جميع ما كان منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The neck is singled out because it is a distinctive body part; something fastened there cannot be escaped.
rows.anchor: إنما ذكر العنق؛ لأنه عضو لا نظير له في (5) الجسد، ومن ألزم بشيء فيه فلا محيد له عنه،

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line about carrying something as a dove's collar illustrates the image of a deed fastened to the neck.
rows.anchor: اذهب بها اذهب بها … طوقتها طوق الحمامة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet saying there is no contagion or augury and every person has his bird attached to his neck.
rows.anchor: لا عدوى ولا طيرة وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A connected report from Jabir has the Prophet say each servant's bird is at his neck.
rows.anchor: طير كل عبد في عنقه

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: The Prophet says each day's deeds are sealed; when a believer is ill, God orders the angels to record his usual deeds until he recovers or dies. Ibn Kathir grades the chain good and strong.
rows.anchor: ليس من عمل يوم إلا وهو يختم عليه، فإذا مرض المؤمن قالت الملائكة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the attached bird as a person's work and the opened book as that work brought out on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: وقال معمر، عن قتادة: {ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} قال: عمله. {ونخرج له يوم القيامة} قال: نخرج ذلك العمل

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan describes two recording angels, one for good deeds and one for sins; after death the closed record accompanies the person in the grave and is opened at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ووكل بك ملكان كريمان، أحدهما عن يمينك والآخر عن يسارك فأما الذي عن يمينك فيحفظ حسناتك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls al-Hasan's description of the record and its accounting a fine piece of speech.
rows.anchor: هذا من حسن (4) كلام الحسن، رحمه الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits the guided person, while misguidance harms the person who strays.
rows.anchor: وزاغ عن سبيل الرشاد، فإنما يجني على نفسه، وإنما يعود وبال ذلك عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul bears another's sin; 29:13 and 16:25 do not contradict this because misleading leaders bear their own misguidance plus the sin of causing others to stray, without reducing those followers' own burden.
rows.anchor: فإن الدعاة عليهم إثم ضلالهم في أنفسهم، وإثم آخر بسبب ما أضلوا من أضلوا من غير أن ينقص من أوزار أولئك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's justice means He does not punish anyone until a messenger establishes the proof; Ibn Kathir cites descriptions of disbelievers admitting messengers warned them.
rows.anchor: وأنه لا يعذب أحدا إلا بعد قيام الحجة عليه بإرسال الرسول إليه، كما قال تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars criticized wording interpolated into Sahih al-Bukhari in connection with 7:56, because it could imply punishment without the required proof.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم طعن جماعة من العلماء في اللفظة التي جاءت مقحمة في صحيح البخاري عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: One report says God creates people for Hell, which then asks for more; Ibn Kathir says this report's wording may have been reversed by a narrator.
rows.anchor: وأنه ينشئ للنار خلقا فيلقون فيها، فتقول: هل من مزيد؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is a realm of grace, but Hell is a realm of justice; no one enters it before warning and proof have been given.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا إنما جاء في الجنة لأنها دار فضل، وأما النار فإنها دار عدل، لا يدخلها أحد إلا بعد الإعذار إليه

rows.speaker: بعض الحفاظ
rows.claim: Some hadith masters suspect the disputed wording was inverted by a transmitter, comparing the sounder versions in which Hell fills only after God places His foot in it and Paradise receives created people.
rows.anchor: وقد تكلم جماعة من الحفاظ في هذه اللفظة (4) وقالوا: لعله انقلب على الراوي بدليل ما أخرجاه في الصحيحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir raises the disputed status of children of disbelievers and of people unable to receive the message, including the mentally disabled, deaf, elderly, and those who died in an interval.
rows.anchor: بقي هاهنا مسألة قد اختلف الأئمة (9) رحمهم الله تعالى، فيها (10) قديما وحديثا وهي: الولدان الذين ماتوا وهم صغار

rows.speaker: الأسود بن سريع
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says four groups will plead on Resurrection Day: the deaf, cognitively impaired, decrepit, and those who died in an interval; they claim no clear call reached them, and are tested by a command to enter the Fire, which would be cool and safe for those who obey.
rows.anchor: أربعة يحتجون يوم القيامة: رجل أصم لا يسمع شيئا، ورجل أحمق، ورجل هرم،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A version from Abu Hurayra says whoever enters the commanded Fire finds it cool and safe, while whoever refuses is dragged to it; al-Bayhaqi calls its chain sound.
rows.anchor: من (3) دخلها كانت عليه بردا وسلاما، ومن لم يدخلها يسحب إليها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Another version says four people each present an argument before God; Ibn Jarir transmits one version as Abu Hurayra's own statement and has him cite this verse.
rows.anchor: أربعة كلهم يدلي على الله بحجة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet says children of polytheists had neither sins to merit punishment nor good deeds for reward, so they will serve the people of Paradise rather than rule there.
rows.anchor: لم يكن لهم سيئات فيعذبوا (10) بها فيكونوا من أهل النار، ولم يكن لهم حسنات فيجازوا بها

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A report says the newborn, cognitively impaired, interval-deceased, and very aged will present their cases; God tests them by commanding them to enter a Fire, and they divide between Paradise and Hell according to their response.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يؤتى بأربعة يوم القيامة: بالمولود، والمعتوه، ومن مات في الفترة، والشيخ الفاني الهرم،

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar also transmits the report about four groups given a test on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: وهكذا رواه الحافظ أبو بكر البزار، عن يوسف بن موسى، عن جرير بن عبد الحميد، بإسناده مثله (1)

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Asked about children of Muslims and polytheists, the Prophet said they are with their parents; when asked what they do, he replied that God knows best.
rows.anchor: قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أطفال المسلمين قال: "هم مع آبائهم". وسئل عن أولاد المشركين فقال: "هم مع آبائهم".

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: A report says people of the pre-Islamic age will plead that no messenger or command reached them; when tested by God's command to enter Hell, they retreat, and the Prophet says first-time obedience would have made it cool and safe.
rows.anchor: فيأمرهم (4) أن يعمدوا إلى جهنم فيدخلوها، فينطلقون حتى إذا دنوا منها وجدوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا،

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar says the wording of Thawban's report is unfamiliar and known only through this particular route.
rows.anchor: ثم قال البزار: ومتن هذا الحديث غير معروف إلا من هذا الوجه، لم يروه عن أيوب إلا عباد،

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معين والنسائي وأبو داود وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: Critics differ on Reyhan ibn Sa'id: Ibn Hibban includes him among reliable transmitters, Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i see no problem, Abu Dawud is dissatisfied, and Abu Hatim says his reports are recorded but not relied upon as proof.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معين والنسائي: لا بأس به، ولم يرضه أبو داود. وقال أبو حاتم: شيخ لا بأس به يكتب حديثه ولا يحتج به.

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: A report has the person who died in an interval, the cognitively impaired, and the child explain their lack of scripture, reason, or maturity; they are tested with a fire, which the fortunate enter and the doomed refuse.
rows.anchor: الهالك في الفترة والمعتوه والمولود: يقول الهالك في الفترة: لم يأتني كتاب،

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar says Abu Sa'id's report is known only through its route from Atiyya, and gives a variant ending in which God says the people disobeyed Him, so how would they have responded to messengers?
rows.anchor: ثم قال: لا يعرف من حديث أبي سعيد إلا من طريقه، عن عطية عنه،

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: A report from Muadh says those tested see bursts of fire and flee twice; God then says He knew their future deeds before creating them and consigns them to the Fire.
rows.anchor: فيقول الرب عز وجل: قبل أن أخلقكم علمت ما أنتم عاملون، وعلى علمي خلقتكم، وإلى علمي تصيرون،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says every child is born upon the natural disposition, while parents make the child Jewish, Christian, or Zoroastrian; an animal is likewise born whole, and God knows what children who die young would have done.
rows.anchor: كل مولود يولد على الفطرة، فأبواه يهودانه وينصرانه ويمجسانه،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the children of Muslims are in Paradise and Ibrahim cares for them.
rows.anchor: ذراري المسلمين في الجنة، يكفلهم إبراهيم عليه السلام (1)

rows.speaker: عياض بن حمار
rows.claim: In a divine report transmitted by Muslim, God says He created His servants as hanifs; another version says “Muslims.”
rows.anchor: إني خلقت عبادي حنفاء

rows.speaker: سمرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says every newborn is born on the natural disposition, including the children of polytheists.
rows.anchor: عن سمرة، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "كل مولود يولد على الفطرة"

rows.speaker: سمرة
rows.claim: A separate report from Samura has the Prophet say that children of polytheists will serve the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن سمرة قال: سألنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أطفال المشركين فقال: "هم خدم أهل الجنة"

rows.speaker: عم حسناء
rows.claim: The Prophet says a prophet, martyr, newborn, and child buried alive are in Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن حسناء (9) بنت معاوية من بني صريم قالت: حدثني عمي قال: قلت: يا رسول الله، من في الجنة؟ قال: "النبي في الجنة، والشهيد في الجنة،

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars suspend judgment about the fate of children of polytheists because reports differ.
rows.anchor: فمن العلماء من ذهب إلى التوقف (11) فيهم لهذا الحديث،

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars confidently place them in Paradise, citing Samura's report in al-Bukhari that Ibrahim was with the children of Muslims and polytheists.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جزم لهم بالجنة، لحديث سمرة بن جندب في صحيح البخاري:

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars confidently place them in Hell, citing the report that they are with their fathers.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جزم لهم بالنار، لقوله عليه السلام (14) : "هم مع آبائهم".

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
rows.claim: The view that children are tested on Resurrection Day, with obedience revealing prior felicity and refusal revealing prior wretchedness, reconciles the evidence; al-Ashari reports it as the Sunni position, and al-Bayhaqi and other hadith scholars defend it.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو الذي حكاه الشيخ أبو الحسن علي بن إسماعيل الأشعري، رحمه الله، عن أهل السنة والجماعة،

rows.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr objects that the testing reports are weak and not probative: the Hereafter is for recompense rather than action, and no one can be required to enter the Fire beyond their capacity.
rows.anchor: وأحاديث هذا الباب ليست قوية، ولا تقوم بها حجة وأهل العلم ينكرونها؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir answers that the reports range from sound to fair, while weaker ones are strengthened together; testing before entry into Paradise or Hell does not contradict the Hereafter being a realm of recompense.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما هو حسن، ومنها ما هو ضعيف يقوى (1) بالصحيح والحسن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As evidence that people can still be tested in the Hereafter, Ibn Kathir cites God's call to prostrate and the authentic reports that believers prostrate while hypocrites cannot.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى: {يوم يكشف عن ساق ويدعون إلى السجود} [ن: 42]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last person to leave Hell is repeatedly bound by promises before God finally permits him to enter Paradise, showing that further commands occur in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين في الرجل الذي يكون آخر أهل النار خروجا منها أن الله يأخذ عهوده ومواثيقه ألا يسأل غير ما هو فيه، ويتكرر ذلك مرارا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test is not beyond human capacity: people must cross the razor-thin bridge over Hell, with believers crossing at different speeds and some falling face-first into the Fire.
rows.anchor: فإن الله يأمر العباد يوم القيامة بالجواز على الصراط، وهو جسر على جهنم أحد من السيف وأدق من الشعرة، ويمر المؤمنون عليه بحسب أعمالهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test resembles the Dajjal's apparent fire, which believers are commanded to enter because it will be cool and safe for them.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فقد ثبتت السنة بأن الدجال يكون معه جنة ونار، وقد أمر الشارع المؤمنين الذين يدركونه أن يشرب أحدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God once commanded the Israelites to kill themselves after worshipping the calf; although severe, that ordeal was no less difficult than the reported test.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإن الله تعالى [قد] (7) أمر بني إسرائيل أن يقتلوا أنفسهم، فقتل بعضهم بعضا حتى قتلوا فيما قيل في غداة واحدة سبعين ألفا،

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: One view places children of polytheists in Paradise, based on Samura's report of them with Ibrahim and the report that a newborn is in Paradise; Ibn Kathir says testing reports are more specific.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنهم في الجنة، واحتجوا بحديث سمرة أنه، عليه السلام (1) رأى مع إبراهيم أولاد المسلمين وأولاد المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reconciles Paradise reports with testing: God places in the barzakh with Ibrahim children already known to obey, while the others' fate is decided by their test at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فمن علم الله [عز وجل] (4) منه أنه يطيع جعل (5) روحه في البرزخ مع إبراهيم وأولاد المسلمين

rows.speaker: بعض القائلين بالجنة
rows.claim: Among those who say the children are in Paradise, some consider them independent inhabitants and others servants, the latter based on a weak report from Anas through Ali ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يجعلهم خدما لهم، كما جاء في حديث علي بن زيد، عن أنس، عند أبي داود الطيالسي (7) وهو ضعيف،

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from Aisha says children follow their fathers; when asked whether this is without deeds, the Prophet answered that God knows what they would have done.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "هم تبع لآبائهم". فقلت: يا رسول الله، بلا عمل؟ فقال: "الله أعلم بما كانوا عاملين" (9)

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Another report has the Prophet say children of believers are with their parents and children of polytheists are with theirs, while God knows what they would have done.
rows.anchor: الله أعلم بما كانوا عاملين

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report transmitted through Bahiyya has Aisha say the Prophet offered to let her hear the cries of polytheist children in the Fire; Ibn Kathir notes that Abu Aqil in its route is abandoned.
rows.anchor: عن مولاته بهية عن عائشة؛ أنها ذكرت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أطفال المشركين فقال: "إن شئت أسمعتك تضاغيهم في النار"
